title: A day in the life of a torque wrench, told by the torque wrench
summary: A click-type torque wrench narrates a day of being used correctly.

blocks.heading: 06:58 · Taken seriously
blocks.body: He opened my case and checked the label before he checked his phone. A promising start. I am a torque wrench. My most important personality trait is being within calibration.

blocks.heading: 09:14 · The click
blocks.body: The fastener was started by hand. He set the specified torque, gripped my handle where he should, and pulled smoothly. I clicked. He stopped. We both enjoyed this rare moment of being understood.

blocks.heading: 11:32 · A difficult conversation
blocks.body: A stubborn bolt appeared. Someone looked at me. I looked, metaphorically, at the breaker bar. We all have gifts. Mine is measuring the end of tightening, not auditioning for demolition.

blocks.heading: 14:06 · Context matters
blocks.body: A different joint came with different instructions: lubricant, tightening sequence, the correct setting. I cannot tell whether a thread is damaged or whether the drawing assumed oil. I measure a turning moment. The person holding me still has to think.

blocks.heading: 16:10 · Back in the case
blocks.body: He followed my manufacturer’s storage instructions and put me away clean and dry. Tomorrow I hope for more of the same: one clear specification, one smooth pull, and nobody deciding that two extra clicks mean extra quality.
